cards.explanation: The answer is fulfill. Jesus says, “I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them.” I know what it feels like to get shoved in a junk drawer, friends, and that is NOT what Jesus is doing with the Law and the Prophets. He's saying they're not going anywhere.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen, will disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.” A jot and a stroke are the smallest marks in the writing. If the little marks stay, you know the big words stay too.

The answer is called great in the kingdom. Jesus says whoever practices and teaches the commandments “…will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.” Notice the two parts, friends, doing it and teaching it. I like that He puts them side by side.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.” Matching them isn't enough, friends. He says it has to exceed theirs.

The answer is angry. Jesus says, “…anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment.” The old command was about murder, and He takes it down to what's going on inside a person. This is the first time He does that, friends, and the rest of the passage follows the same pattern.

The answer is to leave the gift and go reconcile first. Jesus says, “…leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.” The gift waits and the brother gets the first visit. Picture walking out mid-offering, friends. That takes guts.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “Reconcile quickly with your adversary, while you are still on the way to court.” The moment to make peace is on the road, before anyone ever reaches the judge. Waiting is the part He warns about in the next lines, friends.

The answer is the last penny. Jesus says, “…you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.” He doesn't say close enough or most of it, friends. It's the whole amount, down to the final coin.

The answer is heart. Jesus says anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her “…has already committed adultery with her in his heart.” It's the same move as with murder, friends, where He goes from the act to what's inside. This is a serious one, and He means it.

The answer is that it's better to lose one part than your whole body in hell. About the eye, Jesus says, “It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.” About the hand, it's the same idea, with the whole body departing into hell. It's intense language, friends. I think He's showing how serious it is.

The answer is sexual immorality. Jesus says anyone who divorces his wife, “…except for sexual immorality, brings adultery upon her.” That's the one exception He names, friends. It's a heavy topic, and He's careful with every word.
The answer is True. After what they'd heard about keeping their oaths, Jesus says, “…I tell you not to swear at all…” That's a big turn, friends. He's going down to the heart of the matter again.

The answer is King. Jesus says Jerusalem is “…the city of the great King.” Look at the list He builds in Matthew 5:34 and 35, friends: heaven is God's throne and the earth is His footstool. Jerusalem is added right after them, with its own reason attached.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “Nor should you swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.” Your head isn't an exception, friends. He gives the reason Himself: you cannot make a single hair white or black.

The answer is to let your yes be yes and your no be no. Jesus says, “Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’…” No big oath needed, friends, just a plain answer you stand behind. Honestly, that's a lot easier to keep track of.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one.” He says it right after telling them not to swear at all. That's a serious thing to say, friends.

The answer is do not resist him. Jesus says, “…I tell you not to resist an evil person.” They'd heard 'Eye for eye and tooth for tooth,' friends, and He gives them something completely different. That's the same 'You have heard… But I tell you' pattern as the rest of the passage.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also…” That's a hard one, friends. He doesn't say it will be easy. He just says it.
The answer is two. Jesus says, “…if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles.” Do the first mile, then keep walking, friends. I'd be asking for a rest at mile one and a half.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.” The asker and the borrower both get the same open hand. Nobody gets sent to a different line, friends.

The answer is to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you. Jesus says, “…love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you…” They'd heard to hate their enemy, friends, and He flips it. Love and prayer for the very people who persecute them.

The answer is sons. Jesus says to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, “…that you may be sons of your Father in heaven.” It's about being family, friends. Then He points to how the Father acts.
The answer is False. Jesus says the Father “…sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.” It falls on both, friends. Same with the sun, which He causes to rise on the evil and the good.

The answer is that it's nothing more than others already do. Jesus asks, “…what are you doing more than others?” Tax collectors love those who love them, and Gentiles greet their own brothers. So loving only your own isn't going beyond, friends.

The answer is perfect. Jesus says, “Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.” After all that talk about loving enemies, friends, He points to the Father as the example. It's a big word, and it's the word He uses.
